title: System V AMD64 allocates integer class and SSE class parameters separately
summary: For ordinary scalar calls with sufficient registers, integer class parameters and SSE class parameters use their own register sequences independently.
applies: 64-bit native ABI; interprets types and calls based on build target
detail: For example, the parameters of void f(int,double,int) are in EDI, XMM0, and ESI in sequence. Floating point parameters do not consume an integer parameter slot.
boundary: Aggregates must be sorted first; fallback and stack transfer rules must be followed when there are insufficient registers.
relevance: Explain why Linux and Windows debug snapshots of the same prototype cannot be read from the same set of slots.
